solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Met trouble in Congress – explosive stuff

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of the word before it are thrown into a new order
in places the mixed-up letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: congress in its sense of sexual intercourse
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The Metropolitan Police face trouble in Congress over some explosive stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature, but here it is sexual congress. The Met is London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a brand of plastic explosive, so it is literally explosive stuff.

clue.text: One sense in which Garfunkel mounted Blunt

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
in which says the sense holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: sight is one of the five senses
Art Garfunkel, the singer partnered with Paul Simon

explanation.surface: A smutty image of Art Garfunkel mounting someone called Blunt, perhaps the singer James Blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Blunt looks like a name to go with Garfunkel; it is the definition, meaning frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt and straight are synonyms for speaking plainly and honestly, without evasion.

clue.text: Universal, being in dirty film set up, gets discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up lifts it, so the word reads from bottom to top
being in means the letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
a scum is a dirty film on a surface

explanation.surface: A universally rated dirty film somehow ends up producing a discharge.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirty film suggests a pornographic movie, but it is a layer of grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus is a slimy bodily secretion, a typical discharge from the nose or other membranes.

clue.text: Did a Scott, going without sex: – not right being taken advantage of

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the explorer's word goes around the other piece
not removes the letter for the following word from the explorer's word

blocks.note: Captain Scott explored Antarctica
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is dropped
it is a slang word for sex

explanation.surface: Someone imitated Captain Scott by going without sex, which was not right, and was taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: Without is an old word for outside, so here it means around rather than lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exploited is to be used unfairly for someone else's gain, which is being taken advantage of.

clue.text: "Right off Relate": disloyal French leader

indicators.note: off means a letter is taken away from the word that follows

blocks.note: to relate to something is to pertain to it
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Sounds like a slogan about Relate, the British marriage-guidance charity, beside a traitorous French leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate is capitalised to look like the counselling charity, but it is just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshal Pétain led the Vichy regime that collaborated with Nazi Germany, so he is remembered as a traitor.

clue.text: Drink up, bashful, gutless Fanny

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
without its guts a word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
shy, with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A shy, cowardly woman called Fanny is told to drink up.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny looks like a name; in British slang it is a vulgar word for the vulva, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British vulgar slang terms for the female genitals, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Those lost reels describing the Press Complaints Commission?

definitions.note: a description of the body rather than a synonym; the answer is an adjective applied to it

indicators.note: something that reels staggers about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Lost film reels supposedly documenting the Press Complaints Commission.
explanation.walkthrough: The Press Complaints Commission was the British press's self-regulator, widely mocked for having no power to punish newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothless means lacking power to enforce anything, the standard charge against that weak regulator.

clue.text: Virgin operation headed by stupid nit!

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled thinking, so the letters of the next word come out jumbled

blocks.note: nit rearranged
an act is an operation or deed

explanation.surface: An insult: some Virgin company operation is being run by a stupid nit.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin looks like Richard Branson's company; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact here means sexually untouched, a sense of having kept one's virginity.

clue.text: Warlike action from America's leader – time to change course

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the country is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of America
T is the abbreviation for time
to tack is to change course when sailing

explanation.surface: Warlike action by the American president means it is time to change course.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack is an offensive military move, the archetypal act of war.

clue.text: Stupid taking two drugs

blocks.note: crack is a form of cocaine, the first drug
pot is cannabis, the second drug

explanation.surface: Taking two drugs at once is a stupid idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot describes a person or idea that is eccentric and foolish, close to stupid.

clue.text: (& 20dn.) Winner's butt wedged into baby doll? Leads to quick dismissal

indicators.note: a butt is the end of something, so only the last letter of the winner is used
wedged into means the letter is pushed inside the garment's name

blocks.note: the final letter of winner
a baby doll is a skimpy nightdress, a shift being a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: A winner's backside squeezed into a skimpy baby-doll nightie leads to someone being quickly sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: Butt looks like a backside but marks the end of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone short shrift is to dismiss them curtly, with no time or sympathy.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Congress routinely lying: "Ignorant foreigners should be converted"

blocks.note: first meaning: the most conventional way of lying down for sex
second meaning: the stance of a preacher sent abroad to win converts

explanation.walkthrough: Congress routinely lying looks like a jibe at US politicians; it means sex in the usual posture.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the standard face-to-face sexual posture and, literally, a proselytiser's attitude towards foreigners.

clue.text: Murdoch acknowledging concealing an instance of privacy invasion?

indicators.note: concealing says the letters lie tucked within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: the end of Murdoch and the start of acknowledging

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch admits to covering up an invasion of privacy.
explanation.walkthrough: This alludes to the phone-hacking scandal at Murdoch's News of the World.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is an act of breaking into someone's phone or computer, a breach of their privacy.

clue.text: Make the first move sexually, in faith being hard?

indicators.note: in places the letter for the last word inside the word for faith

blocks.note: trust is faith in someone
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Is making the first sexual move hard for someone of religious faith?
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust is to push forward forcefully, here with a sexual undertone of an opening move.

clue.text: Strange start to upper hand fore-play

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken
play means the letters are toyed with and moved around

blocks.note: the first letter of upper
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds foreplay that begins with an upper hand rather strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Fore-play is split: fore is fodder and play is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard of is unprecedented or unknown, and so strange.

clue.text: Bill royally gets a rise screwing (Lewinsky's last but one to go on top)

indicators.note: last but one points to the penultimate letter of the name
screwing twists things around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the seventh, penultimate letter of Lewinsky
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton gets aroused in the Lewinsky affair, with Monica on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like Clinton, but Kaiser Bill was the British nickname for Wilhelm II, the German emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser was the German imperial title, and Kaiser Bill was Wilhelm II's popular nickname, so a royal Bill.

clue.text: Tim, does my bum ... lacking restraint

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: the quality of lacking restraint

indicators.note: bum means poor or wrong, so the letters before it are badly arranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks Tim the classic question 'does my bum look big in this?', trailing off shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is a want of decency or reserve, the quality of behaving without restraint.

clue.text: Time to break balls, time to get into dress – don't hold back

indicators.note: breaking into the balls means the letter splits them apart
to get into means the gathered letters go inside the garment's name

blocks.note: two O shapes look like balls
T is the abbreviation for time
T again for the second time
a gown is a dress

explanation.surface: Time to be ruthless, time to get dressed up and not hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: Put T between the two Os, add T, and place the lot inside GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to town is an idiom for doing something lavishly or with abandon.

clue.text: Like Miliband and colleagues duped into broadcast

indicators.note: into puts one word inside the other

blocks.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it
to be had is to be duped

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband and his team are fooled into going on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast suggests TV, but it means scattering seed. Miliband led Labour in opposition, heading the shadow cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics the opposition's frontbench is the shadow cabinet, so its members are shadow ministers.

clue.text: Ice cream man's wife with big thighs?

definitions.note: the possessive points to the name Whippy, as in Mr Whippy

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
hippy means broad in the hips

explanation.surface: The ice cream man's wife is a well-padded woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Whippy is the British soft-serve ice cream brand sold from vans, so it is the ice cream man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Whippy is the familiar trade name of the British ice cream van, hence the ice cream man's own name.

clue.text: City Kate the model horrible woman, as Bush would say

indicators.note: George W. Bush's American pronunciation is what turns the spoken pieces into the city's name

blocks.note: Kate Moss is the famous model, and cow is an insult for an unpleasant woman

explanation.surface: A city named after a model and a nasty woman, pronounced like the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say the Russian capital as moss-cow, whereas Britons say moss-co.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: see 9ac.
Islamic sect quiet on Iran, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means only the letters in odd positions are kept

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
the first and third letters of Iran

explanation.surface: A sect stays quiet about Iran, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Shia is one of the two main branches of Islam, dominant in Iran.

clue.text: Cut balls off after outing government PR aide?

indicators.note: after sends the castration word second, behind the word for a jaunt

blocks.note: a spin is a short trip or outing
to doctor an animal is to castrate it

explanation.surface: After being outed, someone's career is castrated: a jibe at a disgraced press officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Outing suggests exposure, but it is a jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a political press adviser who puts a favourable slant on news.

clue.text: Number of lives overturned by Times, heartlessly Conservative

indicators.note: overturned turns the word upside down, which in a down clue reads it backwards
without its heart a word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: he lives there means he is there
X is the multiplication sign
Tory with its middle removed

explanation.surface: Some number of lives were ruined by the Times and callous Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a Conservative in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty is a cardinal number, six tens.

clue.text: Whip standing by Cameron initially – hard for Nick

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the name is taken

blocks.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip
the first letter of Cameron
H is the abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The party whip stands by David Cameron, making life hard for Nick Clegg in the coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like Clegg, Cameron's coalition deputy; it is the verb meaning to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick a criminal is to arrest them, that is, catch them.

clue.text: Maybe finger old flame after accepted date

indicators.note: after sends the former partner to the end, behind the other pieces

blocks.note: an idea that is in is accepted or fashionable
D is the abbreviation for date
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone should point the finger at an old flame after a date was accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Maybe marks the definition as an example: one finger is the index.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the forefinger, so a finger may be called an index.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Hard-on doubtful after second time

indicators.note: after sends the word for doubtful to the end, behind the other pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time
iffy means uncertain or doubtful

explanation.surface: A man's erection is doubtful when he tries a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffy is British slang for an erection, the same as a hard-on.

clue.text: Phony, misguided, tense inside – that's Palin for one

indicators.note: misguided means sent the wrong way, so the letters lose their order
inside places the letter within the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Accuses someone of being a phony, misguided and tense, like Sarah Palin.
explanation.walkthrough: Palin suggests Sarah Palin the US politician, but it is Michael Palin of the Monty Python comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Palin was a member of Monty Python, so he is one of the Pythons.
